notes: Modified cash basis village (recorded as cash basis). Governmental lines from Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances - Cash Basis, Total Governmental Funds 2023 column (p6; fund columns p5). Taxes 479,152 split using the General Fund schedule (p10: Property tax 464,137 + Motor vehicle tax 15,015). Intergovernmental revenues 188,671 split using the Schedule 2 Totals column (p11: Highway allocation 87,952, Motor vehicle fees 5,930, Homestead allocation 9,628, Other 85,161). Bond issue costs (800), bond principal (105,000) and bond interest (28,198) are printed under Other financing sources (uses) below Total expenditures, so recorded as disbursements with outside_printed_total. Beginning/ending cash = total cash assets of governmental funds (2022 comparative 2,436,895 and 2023 2,050,652, p4), equal to fund balances. Business-type from the proprietary Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Net Position (p8, single Totals column; modified cash basis with capital assets, depreciation and debt, so measure net position); business-type disbursements total = operating 320,741 + non-operating 48,208. The statement of activities (p2) shows Sewer 70,260 and Water 285,020 expenses but no by-fund proprietary statement. Balance sheet from the government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1) since it includes capital assets and debt; zero-value rows omitted. Detail: Schedule 2 (major funds, p10-11) and Schedule 4 (non-major funds, p12) by fund column, 2023 actual; Schedule 6 (p15) Actual column for proprietary funds; Schedule 5 (p14) prints only fund-type budget totals and is not recorded. Schedule 2 shows charges for services totals 173,894 (major funds) and the Fire Fund's 1,000 is printed as Miscellaneous on p12 but as Charges for services in the statement's non-major column (p6).
